sources.title: Behavioral Changes of Solitary Housed Female Pygmy Slow Lorises (Nycticebus pygmeaus) after Introduction into Group Enclosures
sources.locator: Abstract; Simple Summary; Results and Discussion.
sources.scope: Primary before-and-after captive study of female pygmy slow lorises moved from solitary housing to group enclosures; measured behavior and fecal cortisol. The article uses the earlier genus Nycticebus.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, stated in the PMC record and article open-access notice.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Article front matter: open access under Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license.
sources.attribution: Alejandro J, Yamanashi Y, Nemoto K, et al. (2021). Behavioral Changes of Solitary Housed Female Pygmy Slow Lorises (Nycticebus pygmeaus) after Introduction into Group Enclosures. Animals 11(9):2751. https://doi.org/10.3390/ani11092751. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The study observed captive female pygmy slow lorises before and after transfer from solitary housing into group enclosures, recording behavior and fecal cortisol.
claims.scope: Captive housing transition; the article uses the earlier genus name Nycticebus.

claims.text: Fecal cortisol levels were lower after social housing; one female showed stereotypic behavior while housed alone and no longer showed that behavior after introduction into a group enclosure.
claims.scope: Behavioral and hormonal results for captive female subjects; not evidence of wild social organization or a species-wide hormonal norm.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The study concerns captive housing and does not establish behavior, social organization, habitat, diet, or conservation status in wild populations.
